column1: # Real (type, shape, bytes) triples measured from real GGUF files.
# Method: for each tensor, compute nbytes from the type table, pad to the
# file's declared alignment, and compare to the gap between this tensor's
# declared offset and the next one's. Across 28 files and 2448 tensors the
# two agreed every time. These 20 rows are that result, deduplicated to at
# most two shapes per (type, rank).
# Corpus: C:\Models\gguf-corpus (see its MANIFEST.json for provenance).
# This fixture is self-contained: the test does NOT read the corpus, so it
# passes on a machine that has never downloaded a model.
# Covered here: 14 of 35 live codes. The other 21 appear in no ordinary
# Hub download and are covered by Task 8's authored fixtures instead.
# Honesty note 1: the sabotage this fixture supports demonstrates test
# *sensitivity*, not ground-truth *provenance*. Making Q6_K disagree and
# watching the test go red proves the code and this fixture CAN disagree;
# it does not prove these numbers are right. A fixture whose values had
# secretly been computed by the same block formula the code uses would
# produce an identical-looking red. The independence lives in how these
# numbers were obtained — comparing each computed size against the real
# gap between consecutive tensor offsets in actual files — and that
# comparison happened off-repo and cannot be re-run from this checkout.
# Treat "differential" as a description of that offline method, not as a
# claim of a third source auditable from this repo.
# Honesty note 2: this test gives the `alignment` column zero coverage.
# `Encoding::byte_size` computes (elem_count / elements_per_block) *
# bytes_per_block and never consults `BlockSpec::alignment`. "Padded to
# the file's declared alignment" above is GGUF's file-level
# general.alignment (default 32) — a different thing from the per-type
# struct alignment (1, 2, or 4) carried in the type table. Nothing in
# this crate cross-checks the per-type alignment column against real
# bytes.
